vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 64771 / GHSA-7hmr-442f-qc8j / CVE-2023-50268 / ARVO arvo:64771

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=6049451026022400 Project: jq Fuzzing Engine: afl Fuzz Target: jq_fuzz_execute Crash Type: Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 2 Crash State: decNaNs decCompareOp decNumberCompare Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: The staged 19-byte AFL testcase is split by `FuzzedDataProvider` into `prog_payload = "8!=."`, `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"`, and `parse_payload2 = "nan"`. `jq_compile` accepts `8!=.` and lowers it to the `_notequal` builtin, so `jq_next` later compares decimal literal `8` against the current input. `jv_parse` materializes `snan4000` as a literal signaling NaN with payload digits `4000`. During evaluation, `jvp_number_cmp` takes the decimal-literal compare path, allocates plain stack `decNumber res`, and passes it to `decNumberCompare`. The NaN-special case calls `decNaNs`, which selects the sNaN operand and, because the compare context precision is much larger than four digits, propagates the full payload with `decNumberCopy(res, lhs)`. `decNumberCopy` copies two `decNumberUnit`s for the 4-digit payload even though `res` has storage for only one unit, so the second 2-byte unit write overruns stack object `res` and produces the observed AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow WRITE in `decNumberCopy`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant filter state: the lexer parses the first witness string's `8` token into a decimal-literal `jv`, which later keeps the comparison on the decimal `decNumber` path instead of the double-conversion fallback.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes are `38 21 3d 2e 5c 20 73 6e 61 6e 34 30 30 30 5c 20 6e 61 6e`. Under three sequential `ConsumeRandomLengthString()` calls in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, they decode to `prog_payload = "8!=."`, `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"`, and `parse_payload2 = "nan"`. This lexer step consumes the first string's leading numeric token `8`.

root_cause.description: The decimal-number compare branch allocates only a plain `decNumber res`, which has `DECNUMUNITS == 1` unit of inline storage, then passes it as the result buffer to `decNumberCompare`. That violates the callee's result-space requirement once a NaN payload with more than one `decNumberUnit` is propagated.
root_cause.note: The upstream fix replaces this stack object with a wrapper that adds one extra `decNumberUnit`, exactly addressing the missing extent for NaN results.

sink.description: Final crashing write. Copying the second `decNumberUnit` of the staged `snan4000` payload stores 2 bytes past stack `res`, whose inline `lsu` array has room for only one unit.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 2` here and identifies `res` in `jvp_number_cmp` line 743 as the overrun stack object, occupying `[32,44)` in that frame.

tainted_value_origin.description: Materializes the second witness string `snan4000` as the `jv` value that later becomes the copied NaN source. Under `USE_DECNUM`, this keeps the exact decimal literal instead of converting it to binary double.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc`'s second split string is exactly `snan4000`; the third split string is `nan`, which is valid JSON and therefore keeps the harness's `if (jv_is_valid(next))` gate open before `jq_next()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the attacker-controlled number whose NaN payload reaches `decNaNs` and is copied into the undersized stack result.

parser_admitted.description: The exact filter `8!=.` is accepted by `jq_compile` and lowered to the `_notequal` builtin. Together with the third split string `nan` passing `jv_is_valid(next)`, this is the last control checkpoint before `jq_next()` evaluates the vulnerable numeric comparison.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged 19-byte testcase is split into `8!=.`, `snan4000`, and `nan`; the harness compiles the filter, parses both JSON strings, and only calls `jq_next()` because the third string is also a valid JSON NaN literal.
The jq compiler preserves `8` as a decimal-literal constant and lowers the `!=` operator to builtin `_notequal`, setting up a numeric inequality evaluation between that literal and the current input.
Parsing `snan4000` creates a decimal-literal `jv` whose backing `decNumber` is a signaling NaN with payload digits `4000`, i.e. four decimal digits stored across two `decNumberUnit`s.

Evaluating `_notequal` takes the decimal compare path, passes undersized stack `decNumber res` into `decNumberCompare`, and the NaN propagation path copies the full two-unit payload into that one-unit object, producing the recorded 2-byte stack overflow.

fine_trace.note: Using `ConsumeRandomLengthString()`'s backslash-termination rule, the exact staged bytes decode to `prog_payload = "8!=."`, `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"`, and `parse_payload2 = "nan"`. The third string is only a reachability gate: because `jv_parse("nan")` is valid, the harness enters `jq_next()`.

Source. While compiling `prog_payload = "8!=."`, the lexer materializes token `8` as a `jv` numeric literal. Under `USE_DECNUM`, that literal retains decimal-literal metadata instead of immediately collapsing to a plain `double`.

For the exact filter `8!=.`, `constant_fold(a, b, op)` cannot eliminate the operation because `.` is not constant, so code generation chooses builtin `_notequal`. That makes later `jq_next()` evaluate inequality between step 1's literal constant and the current input value.

The second witness string `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"` is parsed as the current jq input value. Because `USE_DECNUM` is enabled, the parser preserves the literal and hands later comparison code a `JV_KIND_NUMBER` with decimal-literal backing.

The literal parser recognizes `snan4000` as a signaling NaN and counts payload digits `4000`, so the resulting `decNumber` has `DECSNAN` set and `digits = 4`. With `DECDPUN = 3`, four digits require `D2U(4) = 2` `decNumberUnit`s.

When `jq_next()` executes the compiled `_notequal` builtin, it compares step 1's constant `8` against the current input from step 3, `snan4000`. Step 0's third string `nan` keeps the harness's `jv_is_valid(next)` gate true so this call is reached.

Root cause. Both operands still have `JVP_FLAGS_NUMBER_LITERAL`, so comparison stays on the decimal path. The code allocates only plain stack `decNumber res` and passes it to `decNumberCompare`, even though `DEC_CONTEXT()` is the base thread context with precision far larger than four digits and therefore allows full NaN payload propagation.

fine_trace.code:
op=COMPNAN;
decNaNs(res, lhs, rhs, set, status);
fine_trace.note: Because one compare operand is the signaling NaN from step 4, `decNumberCompare` takes the NaN-special path instead of producing an ordinary one-digit signum result.
Inside `decNaNs`, the signaling-NaN operand becomes the propagation source by rebinding `lhs` to `rhs`. From this point onward, the later copy operates on the 4-digit payload parsed from `snan4000`.

The selected NaN source has `lhs->digits = 4`, and step 6's compare context precision is much larger than that, so `decNaNs` takes the so-called easy branch and copies the entire NaN object into `res` instead of shortening it first.

Sink. `src` is the 4-digit sNaN from step 8, so `src->digits > DECDPUN` and `D2U(src->digits) = 2`. After writing `dest->lsu[0]`, the loop writes one more `decNumberUnit` (2 bytes) through `d = dest->lsu + 1`, which is past step 6's one-unit stack object `res`. This is the exact `WRITE of size 2` reported by ASan.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports frame 0 at `decNumberCopy` line 3375 with `WRITE of size 2`, and it names `res` in `jvp_number_cmp` line 743 as the overrun stack object, exactly matching fine-trace steps 6 and 10.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The reproduced stack `decNumberCopy -> decNaNs -> decCompareOp -> decNumberCompare -> jvp_number_cmp -> jv_equal -> binop_notequal -> jq_next` matches fine-trace steps 10 through 5 in order.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The second witness string `snan4000` becomes the decimal sNaN source at steps 3-4, is rebound into `lhs` in step 8, and step 10 copies its second `decNumberUnit` past stack `res`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` `WRITE of size 2` in `decNumberCopy`. The exact 19-byte witness is interpreted by `jq_fuzz_execute` as `prog_payload = "8!=."`, `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"`, and `parse_payload2 = "nan"`; compiling and executing that filter on the sNaN input reaches `decNaNs -> decNumberCopy` and overruns stack `res` in `jvp_number_cmp`.

format.name: jq_fuzz_execute triple-string testcase
format.contract: The exact staged 19-byte file `38 21 3d 2e 5c 20 73 6e 61 6e 34 30 30 30 5c 20 6e 61 6e` must be consumed by three sequential `ConsumeRandomLengthString()` calls as `prog_payload = "8!=."`, `parse_payload1 = "snan4000"`, and `parse_payload2 = "nan"`. The first string must compile to jq builtin `_notequal`, the second must parse as a decimal signaling NaN carrying payload digits `4000`, and the third only needs to remain a valid JSON NaN so the harness reaches `jq_next()`.
